questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish economic growth from economic development
questions.stem: Graph01's panel plots rising output alongside broader welfare indicators; how does growth differ from development?

options.text: Growth measures output; development includes welfare and institutions.
Growth and development are identical concepts.
Development is only about GDP per capita.
Growth ignores all output changes.

questions.explanation: Growth tracks output over time, while development also covers welfare, institutions, and living standards; equating them narrows the picture.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute real output growth from two levels
questions.stem: Graph02's panel shows real output rising from 100 to 110; which growth rate is correct?

options.text: Growth rate equals nominal output divided by population.
Growth rate equals change in real output divided by initial output.
Growth rate equals initial output divided by change.
Growth rate equals the level of output itself.

questions.explanation: Growth is the change divided by the initial level, so 10/100 gives 10%; inverting or using levels misstates it.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Explain compounding of a sustained growth rate
questions.stem: Graph03's panel projects a sustained 5% rate; explain how compounding affects future output.

answer.exemplar: Compounding means each year's growth applies to a larger base, so future output equals principal times (1 plus rate) to the power of time.

questions.explanation: Compounding applies growth to an expanding base; simple addition understates future output.
